definitions.explanation: Expressing that something is impressive, remarkable, or extraordinary. Very commonly used in casual conversation.
Originally meant something frightening or extreme (can still be used this way).

examples.japanese: すごい！⟦{上手|じょうず}→上手：00707_jouzu⟧⟦です→です：09485_desu⟧⟦ね→ね：09474_ne⟧。
examples.english: Amazing! You're so good at it.

examples.japanese: すごい⟦{人|ひと}→人：00476_hito⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦たくさん→たくさん：00597_takusan⟧⟦います→いる：00495_iru⟧⟦ね→ね：09474_ne⟧。
⟦あの→あの：00915_ano⟧⟦{映画|えいが}→映画：02273_eiga⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧すごかった。

⟦{彼女|かのじょ}→彼女：01286_kanojo⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{語学|ごがく}→語学：02770_gogaku⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{才能|さいのう}→才能：02772_sainou⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧すごくて、⟦{五|ご}→五：00697_go⟧か⟦{国語|こくご}→国語：02739_kokugo⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧⟦{話|はな}せる→話す：00467_hanasu⟧んだって。
examples.english: She has an incredible talent for languages—apparently she can speak five languages.

examples.japanese: ⟦{台風|たいふう}→台風：01455_taifuu⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{風|かぜ}→風：00641_kaze⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧すごくて、⟦{外|そと}→外：00671_soto⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{出|で}られなかった→出る：00513_deru⟧。⟦{木|き}→木：00524_ki⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧{何本|なんぼん}⟦か→か：09473_ka⟧⟦{倒|たお}れた→倒れる：01160_taoreru⟧⟦らしい→らしい：09502_rashii⟧。
examples.english: The typhoon winds were terrible, so we couldn't go outside. Apparently several trees fell over too.

examples.japanese: すごい⟦{景色|けしき}→景色：01395_keshiki⟧⟦だ→だ：09496_da⟧⟦ね→ね：09474_ne⟧！
⟦{雨|あめ}→雨：00583_ame⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧すごくて⟦{出|で}られない→出る：00513_deru⟧。
examples.english: The rain is so bad I can't go out.
There was a terrible noise—what was that?

examples.japanese: ⟦{渋滞|じゅうたい}→渋滞：03279_juutai⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧すごかった。

notes: すごい conjugates as an i-adjective: すごくない (negative), すごくて (te-form), すごかった (past). The kanji {凄|すご}い can be used but hiragana is more common. In casual speech, すごく is often used as an intensifier meaning 'very' (e.g., すごくおいしい - very delicious). Young people often say すげー as a casual variant.
